# Rule evidence (auto-generated by `python -m app.report`)

Every threshold below is computed from the 50-case portfolio, not chosen by hand.

## Method

1. **Natural breaks.** For each continuous signal the sorted values are split into 3 groups (baseline / elevated / extreme) by minimising within-group variance (Jenks, k=3, exact DP). The threshold is the midpoint of the empty gap between adjacent groups, so it sits where the real distribution has no cases.
2. **Rule levels.** Crossing the *elevated* break = MEDIUM, crossing the *extreme* break = HIGH. Binary flags are HIGH except `recent_policy_change_flag` (LOW: 12/50 and weak on its own).
3. **Domains.** Signals are grouped into Billing / Utilization / Geography / Relationship / Timing. In this data the signals co-move (the 8 worst cases trip *everything*), so summing rules would double-count. The score takes the strongest rule per domain and combines domains with noisy-OR: `score = 1 - prod(1 - w_domain)`, weights LOW=5, MEDIUM=12, HIGH=25, CRITICAL=40.
4. **Baseline anomaly (0-10).** Mean percentile rank of the continuous signals, blended in so clean cases still get a stable order.
5. **Bands.** >=80 CRITICAL, >=50 HIGH, >=25 MEDIUM, >=0 LOW. Each cut falls inside an empty stretch of the scored portfolio (no case scores between the two neighbours): CRITICAL cut 80: nearest scores 77.1 | 84.8; HIGH cut 50: nearest scores 38.8 | 52.4; MEDIUM cut 25: nearest scores 5.0 | 27.1.

## Rule catalog

| ID | Rule | Domain | Logic | Fires on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | Duplicate service billed | Billing | binary flag -> HIGH | 13/50 |
| R02 | Service overlaps another provider | Geography | binary flag -> HIGH | 10/50 |
| R03 | Shared contact info with provider | Relationship | binary flag -> HIGH | 12/50 |

| R05 | Weekly visit frequency | Utilization | visits/wk >=5.5 MEDIUM, >=10 HIGH | 18/50 |
| R06 | Member-provider distance | Geography | miles >=47 MEDIUM, >=160.0 HIGH | 14/50 |
| R07 | Amount vs peer average | Billing | % vs peer >=16 MEDIUM, >=76 HIGH | 18/50 |
| R08 | Round-dollar billing ratio | Billing | round-dollar >=0.29 MEDIUM, >=0.62 HIGH | 18/50 |
| R09 | Weekend billing ratio | Billing | weekend ratio >=0.17 MEDIUM, >=0.42 HIGH | 19/50 |
| R10 | Prior claims (12 mo) | Utilization | prior claims >=2.5 MEDIUM, >=7.0 HIGH | 17/50 |
| R11 | Implied weekly travel miles | Geography | miles/wk >=1800.0 HIGH, >=4510.0 CRITICAL | 8/50 |
| R12 | High-value claim | Billing | log-amount robust z >=0.72 MEDIUM (HIGH if >= p90 $32645) | 15/50 |
| R13 | Multi-domain convergence | Convergence | >=3 domains HIGH, >=4 CRITICAL | 16/50 |
| R14 | Silent drift (no flags, many elevated signals) | Convergence | 0 flags and >=3 elevated continuous signals -> MEDIUM | 3/50 |
| R15 | Claim number reused across cases | Integrity | same claim_number on >1 case -> HIGH | 2/50 |
| R17 | Lookalike of a confirmed-fraud case | Precedent | within the median nearest-neighbour distance of a human-confirmed FRAUD case: 1 -> MEDIUM, 2+ -> HIGH (never bulk-clearable) | 0/50 |
| R16 | High-value claim after policy change | Timing | policy change and amount >= p75 ($13131) -> MEDIUM | 10/50 |

Derived-feature rationale:

- **R11 implied weekly travel miles** = visits/wk x distance x 2. Baseline cases stay below ~1.3k; the 8 worst cases sit at 2.3k-7.5k (a member or provider covering thousands of miles a week is physically implausible).
- **R13 convergence** counts domains tripped at >= MEDIUM. Because signals co-move, independent-domain convergence is the strongest evidence.
- **R14 silent drift.** Of the zero-flag cases, 30 trip none of the 7 continuous signals and 3 (C1026, C1040, C1042) trip five; nothing in between. A flag-count model scores those 3 as clean. Threshold = 3 (midpoint of the empty gap).
- **R15 claim-number reuse.** `LTC-2034786` appears on C1001 (benign profile) and C1031 (critical profile) -- a data-integrity lead that no per-row rule can see.
- Not derivable (documented gap): days since policy change (only a 0/1 flag), provider identity, member identity, diagnosis.

Cases with score < 10: 29 (all have zero rules fired).

## Caveats

- Thresholds are calibrated to a 50-row synthetic sample. There are **no fraud labels**, so precision/recall cannot be claimed; in production the weights and breaks should be re-fit against confirmed outcomes.
- The 3-tier structure (8 / ~9 / 33) is very clean because the data is synthetic; real portfolios are continuous, which is why the LLM judge and human review sit on top of the rules rather than replacing them.
